speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help diagnose your vision issues, can you tell me if the black spots are moving like floaters or if they are stationary shadows in your peripheral vision? Also, have you experienced any eye pain or sensitivity to light?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of AIDS and prior fungal esophagitis, I suspect an opportunistic infection. REQUEST TEST: Fundoscopy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Granular yellow-white opacities around the retinal vessels and multiple areas of dot-blot hemorrhages

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Decreased vision and black spots in the right eye. I also have No pain, Left eye is asymptomatic. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: Tuberculosis typically presents with pain and inflammation, which contradicts your painless symptoms and the fundoscopy findings likely showing cotton-wool spots. Given your AIDS status and prior fungal infections, I strongly suspect Toxoplasmosis or CMV retinitis, so I need to rule out active retinal necrosis. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: AIDS, fungal esophagitis treated with fluconazole, Kaposi's sarcoma Social history: No additional information provided

speaker: Doctor
text: The images show characteristic "pizza pie" retinitis with hemorrhages and exudates, which is classic for CMV retinitis in an AIDS patient. DIAGNOSIS READY: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis
